Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
Issued by National Weather Service Corpus Christi TX
651 PM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Generally hot and dry through the end of the week, with heat
  index values close to Heat Advisory thresholds.

- Isolated showers are possible along the sea breeze boundary 
  today and tomorrow.

- Scattered showers and thunderstorms return to the forecast this
  weekend and early next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1200 PM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

Our main concern today will be heat and humidity resulting in heat 
index values that are very close to our Heat Advisory threshold.
We have decided to not issue an advisory today with the latest
forecast update, and here is some of our reasoning. It looks like
temperatures will climb into the upper 90s once again today--very
similar to yesterday. Also similar to yesterday, the boundary 
layer should deepen and sufficiently mix surface dew points into 
the low 70s, perhaps the upper 60s for a few locations across the 
west/northwest portions of our forecast area. This will result in 
heat index values between 105-107 for most locations, with a few 
spots meeting criteria (108-109) for an hour or two. The locations 
that are forecast to meet criteria are isolated and generally more
sheltered. Due to the splotchiness of locations just reaching 
criteria, we did not feel it necessary to issue an advisory in
this situation. We will continue to assess current data and 
adjust as necessary.

It's worth noting that we're still forecasting heat index values
between 105-108. At the end of the day, the human body and an
animal's response to heat does not vary much between 107 and 
108...therefore proper heat safety messaging and precautions 
should continue to be taken regardless of the presence of an 
advisory or not.

Aside from the heat, we have 10-20% PoPs over eastern Harris
county this afternoon and areas extending north of the Houston 
Metro near sunset. It looks like a seabreeze circulation will
develop off the Gulf and Galveston Bay that should provide enough 
low-level convergence to trigger an isolated shower or two this 
afternoon from about 4-8 pm. Forecast soundings indicate a
sufficiently moist/unstable boundary layer to support shallow
showers, but individual updrafts should not be strong enough to
overcome a capping inversion around 700mb/10kft, as well as the
strong subsidence and dry-air entrainment aloft. Therefore, we
only mention a slight-chance of showers in the official forecast 
and capped thunderstorm chances at less than 15%. A similar setup
is forecast tomorrow, so we have similar PoP/precip trends for 
tomorrow afternoon as well.

Thursday and Friday's weather will be quite similar to today (and
yesterday and the day before that) with temperatures in the upper
90s and heat index values between 105-108 for most locations. The
stagnant weather pattern should start to break down as we head
into the weekend. The surface high to our southeast and intense 
mid- and upper-level ridge/high to our northwest will give way to 
a trough over the eastern CONUS early next week. As this ridge
breaks down, a backdoor cold front is forecast to slide into 
Southeast Texas this weekend. We use the world cold very loosely, 
since there won't be much a cool-down (we go from the upper 90s to
the mid 90s) with it. It should at least bring increased rain
chances to the region. Unfortunately rain chances are only around 
20-30% for most of the area, with 50+% PoPs further east toward 
the Golden Triangle. There is a chance that the upper trough digs 
more south than southeast, which would nudge those 50+% PoPs west
into our forecast area, but only about 25% of the global guidance  
is favoring this solution at this time. The global guidance is in
agreement that the front will not be here for a long time and wash 
out/lift north as we head into early next week with a more staunch
fetch of southerly flow blowing across the region. This pattern
usually results in temperatures in the mid/upper 90s with daily 
diurnal seabreeze induced shower/storm chances.

Bonnette

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 648 PM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

VFR conditions across all terminals this evening is expected to 
continue through the overnight hours with some lower clouds starting 
to build around 08Z. Generally expecting MVFR CIGs around 13-14Z 
mainly across northern terminals (UTS/CLL/CXO) due to low confidence 
elsewhere have opted to leave out of TAFs for other sites. Winds 
overnight through early afternoon should be light and variable with 
south to southwesterly winds up to around 10-11KT through the 
evening hours.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1200 PM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

Light to moderate onshore flow and 2 to 4 foot seas will continue
for most of the week. Winds may become more southerly during the
afternoon and hours. Southwesterly winds increase and seas build 
somewhat over the weekend, which may prompt the issuance of 
caution flags. We also expect an increase chance of isolated to 
scattered showers and thunderstorms by the weekend and early next 
week.

Bonnette

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
1234 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, MARINE, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat continues through Saturday with afternoon highs in 
the mid 90s to near 100 and heat indices of 105-110F.

- The Heat Advisory has been expanded to include all of southeast 
Texas and southwest, Central and south central Louisiana this 
afternoon.

- A few showers may develop this afternoon. Better precipitation
  chances return Sunday with afternoon pop up thunderstorms
  expected each day next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(Today through Wednesday)
Issued at 1228 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Persistence is the forecast philosophy in the short 
term as a strong upper level ridge remains in place across much of 
the southwest and south central conus. Despite this, a sliver of 
higher moisture extending from the southeast Louisiana coast up 
through the Dakotas will offer a low end chance (20%) for a couple 
of afternoon showers or thunderstorms across south central Louisiana 
this afternoon. For the rest of us, the heat remains on with 
afternoon highs climbing into the mid to upper 90s with afternoon 
heat indices in the 105-112 range. The Heat Advisory has been 
expanded west with this package to now include all of southeast 
Texas and southwest Louisiana. 

Little movement to the upper ridging will keep conditions largely 
uniform through Saturday. The ridge finally retreats west Saturday 
night into Sunday as an upper level trough and a rare weak surface 
frontal boundary digs through the central U.S. Guidance is very 
split on whether the frontal boundary will reach the coast and even 
if it does, the effect on sensible weather this far south will be 
minimal with perhaps a few degrees drop in dewpoints. The boundary 
will, however, increase PoPs Saturday night into Sunday bringing the 
first appreciable rains to most of the region in over a week. As the 
boundary stalls out and dissipates, a weak gradient aloft will allow 
for diurnally driven afternoon convection to develop each day next 
week. The added cloud cover and precip will keep afternoon highs 
closer to climatological normals in the lower 90s with max heat 
indices from 100-105.

Jones

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 1228 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Weak surface high pressure over the southeastern gulf and ridging
aloft over the south central U.S. will maintain VFR conditions
through the period with light southwesterly winds. 

A technical issue with the AEX visibility sensor is causing it to 
incorrectly report sub optimal visibility. AEX ATC confirms that 
while there is occasional light HZ, the instrument does not 
presently reflect realistic visibilities.

Jones

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1228 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Light winds and low seas are anticipated through Saturday. 
A weak boundary will drift to near the northern gulf coast Saturday 
night into Sunday which will increase winds to 15-20 knots over the 
coastal waters. The boundary will also increase thunderstorm 
chances. Light southerly flow becomes reestablished Monday through 
the rest of the week.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1228 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Hot and humid conditions will continue through the 
end of next week. Rain chances will increase Saturday night into 
Sunday as an upper level trough and weak frontal boundary approach 
the area. A brief period of northwesterly winds could develop 
Sunday, but will quickly turn back out of the south Sunday night 
into Monday. Scattered afternoon thunderstorms will develop each day 
next week.
